name: Eleazar
overview: Eleazar was a male warrior known as the second of "the thirty" mighty men who served King David. He is identified as the son of Dodo, and while his tribal affiliation is not recorded, his role as one of David's elite soldiers marks him as a significant figure in the military history of Israel. No additional notes are provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Eleazar means "G-d is a help," reflecting a trust in divine assistance. This proper name is recorded in 2 Samuel 23:9 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eleazar as the son of Dodo, according to 2 Samuel 23:9. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Eleazar's importance lies in his position as one of David's thirty mighty men, specifically the second in rank among them, highlighting his valor and loyalty in David's military campaigns. His inclusion in this elite group underscores the strength and faithfulness of David's followers during a formative period in Israel's history. His name's meaning further points to reliance on God's help in accomplishing great feats.
